---
title: "Scatter with a continuous colour legend"
description: "A point mark encoding a third variable to colour, with a trained continuous scale and guide."
categories: [Basics]
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("_helper.R")
```

Every plot starts from a data frame with `vplot()`, then adds marks with the
native pipe. Here a `mark_point()` encodes `hp` to colour, and
`scale_color_continuous()` trains the scale and draws the guide.

```{r}
p <- vplot(mtcars) |>
  mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = hp) |>
  scale_color_continuous()
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
vg(p, "scatter-color")
```

## Squishing the outliers into the scale

A handful of extreme values can use up most of a colour ramp. Set the scale's
`limits` to the range you care about and `oob = "squish"` clamps everything
outside it onto the end colours, so the two 300+ hp cars read as "the most
powerful" instead of stretching the palette for everyone else.

The legend can also sit inside the panel when there is empty space for it:
`theme(legend.position = "inside")` with `legend.position.inside` as fractions
of the panel area. The justification follows the position, so `c(0.98, 0.98)`
tucks the legend into the top-right corner.

```{r}
p_squish <- vplot(mtcars) |>
  mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = hp, size = 3) |>
  scale_color_continuous(limits = c(50, 250), oob = "squish") |>
  theme(legend.position = "inside",
        legend.position.inside = c(0.98, 0.98))
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
vg(p_squish, "scatter-color-squish")
```
